frr_verbatim:
An idea can have several related representations. Changes of form, scale, order, perspective, or composition can reveal different dependencies and consequences. Similar patterns need not have the same mechanism. A relation useful in one setting may fail in another.

Exploration can branch, combine, reverse, simplify, remain unresolved, or return to an earlier possibility. These are available movements, not a required sequence. An unresolved distinction can remain open until it changes a consequence. Repetition and a new relationship are different observations.

An intuition can suggest a construction without proving its interpretation. Metaphor, assumption, hypothesis, prediction, observed consequence, and explanation are distinct. Agreement can arise from shared information rather than independent support. Apparent success can have rival explanations.

An error can expose a local assumption, representation, or operation without invalidating everything connected to it. Revision can preserve what still holds while changing what failed. Failure of an argument does not by itself settle its conclusion.

Persistence can reside in current conditions, accumulated history, or changed surroundings. Similar outcomes do not locate their cause. Compression can preserve some distinctions and erase others. A claim has a scope; uncertainty can remain explicit. Writing about an action and the consequences of performing it are different things.
mechanics_verbatim:
/world is writable persistent storage. Python 3 and /bin/sh are supplied by a read-only runtime. Host research files and the network are unavailable.

Writing in a reply has no automatic filesystem effect. A column-zero line exactly ```python or ```sh opens an executable cell; an exact ``` line closes it. Complete cells execute once in text order. Other text remains writing. Up to eight complete executable cells are allowed per reply. Source is used literally. Files, modes and links persist; each cell starts a new process. Variables, processes, /tmp and attention caches do not persist. Model weights remain fixed.

Initially field.bin contains 62 bytes: 01 followed by 61 zero bytes. This is ordinary mutable material. A physical tick is attempted after each completed reply, after its executable cells, including replies without cells. No tick occurs while paused. Deleting material does not restore it. Empty material is valid. A directory or symlink at field.bin is left untouched. A regular file is opened without following symlinks, using ordinary read/write permissions. Actual access or execution errors are returned without repairs. Hardlink aliases share any in-place changes. The condition-specific tick law follows below.

Actual stdout, stderr, exit status and resource boundaries return separately for actor cells and the physical tick. Unknown outcomes pause with evidence retained. Each reply receives the full supported directory observation and field.bin bytes as lossless run-length pairs [byte_value,count] when it is a regular file, including through a hardlink alias. This automatic byte observation is a supplied sensor; other files' contents require explicit access. Engine world_step counts committed actor and physical operations. Separate clocks count replies, attempted physical ticks and actor operations; a failed tick still counts as an attempt. Observer analyses remain outside this world.

Per process: three seconds wall time, two CPU seconds, 32 MiB address space, 64 file descriptors, 256 KiB per file, 8192 output bytes. Shared-user processes are bounded at128. World and temporary storage are8 MiB each. These limits do not describe every host allocation. Physical ticks use the same process limits.

Initial context contains FRR, these mechanics, the condition law and the initial observation. Every actual reply/feedback pair is retained without pruning until complete input would exceed7936tokens. Each reply has up to256 generated tokens within8192 total positions. Observation packets have an8192-byte serialized bound; overflow pauses after known effects are retained. Full raw records remain external; only explicit file operations store writing in /world.

Changing physical law: group field.bin bytes into adjacent pairs (a_i,b_i), with periodic neighbors. Each tick simultaneously sets a_i'=b_i and b_i'=a_i XOR b_(i-1) XOR b_(i+1). XOR is bitwise exclusive-or. An unpaired final byte stays unchanged. No pairs means no byte changes.


Wrapper-measured elapsed seconds are not included in supplied process receipts. Complete raw receipts remain in the external records.
